stories.title: Many women have never discussed heart health with a clinician, and most report multiple symptoms
stories.summary: Heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, and the risk rises during the menopause years. But an international study has revealed that only half of women know this. Many have never talked about their heart with a doctor or a nurse, and the majority are living with multiple symptoms.

stories.title: Cold Triggers a Hidden Molecular Pathway That Extends Lifespan, Study Finds
stories.summary: Can we harness this? ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.

stories.title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say
stories.summary: Chomping on vegtable skins, seeds and stalks could give us vital fibre, say food scientists.

stories.title: The parts of fruits and vegetables most throw away could save your health—and the planet
stories.summary: Most of us routinely discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables at mealtime. But new research from King's College London suggests these scraps could be a valuable—and overlooked—source of dietary fiber, offering potential benefits for both public health and the environment.

stories.title: Manosphere and online misogyny should be treated as public health issues, say UK experts
stories.summary: Report calls for an effort to tackle harms in similar way to obesity and smoking, and stresses need to ‘offer boys something better’ The manosphere and online misogyny should be treated by the government as a public health issue, in the same way as obesity or smoking, experts have said.

stories.title: Could a few bad dietary choices worsen your next immune response?
stories.summary: Scientists have long known that diet shapes the immune system. Now, a UC San Francisco team has found that even a brief dietary change can substantially change how the body responds to skin irritation, at least in mice.

stories.title: When things go bump in the night: How our brains trick us into hearing things that aren't there
stories.summary: It's 3 a.m. You've woken from a dead sleep because you've heard a thud in the darkness or a floorboard creaking downstairs. Or perhaps you've woken because you have the unmistakable sensation you're not alone.

stories.title: Tumor mutations and immune activity may reveal who benefits from investigational lymphoma drug
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Tsukuba conducted a physician-initiated phase 2 clinical trial of dasatinib in patients with relapsed or refractory T-follicular helper cell lymphoma (TFHL), an aggressive and difficult-to-treat blood cancer.

stories.title: Heat waves and pollution increase stroke risk in older adults, study finds
stories.summary: A study conducted in Brazil by researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) found that each additional day spent under a heat wave in São Paulo is associated with an increased risk of acute stroke in people ages 65 and older.

stories.title: Healthy diet may lower heart disease risk after cancer
stories.summary: Eating a healthy diet is associated with a reduced risk of heart disease and death among cancer survivors, according to a study published today in JACC: Advances.

stories.title: Antibody candidate could help preserve appetite and muscle strength in patients with cancer
stories.summary: In cancer cachexia, patients continue to lose weight, muscle and fat even when they eat. A KAIST research team has developed a therapeutic candidate that blocks a signal responsible for appetite suppression, weight loss and excessive energy expenditure.

stories.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that people consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging.

stories.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a new policy for compounding peptides, a PBM disclosure rule, and more
stories.summary: HHS released a policy that will temporarily allow compounding pharmacies to manufacture some peptide products

stories.title: New blood test can detect changes associated with Alzheimer's disease
stories.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease can be detected by a new type of blood test -- and a growing number of patients are asking their doctors about it.

stories.title: NHS Western Isles prescribing weight loss drugs at triple the rate of other health boards
stories.summary: A new report finds "significant variation" between Scotland's health boards prescribing new medicines.

stories.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about 340B battles, new results for a Lilly weight loss drug, and more
stories.summary: Missouri attorney general warned Eli Lilly to discontinue requiring hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under 340B program

stories.title: STAT+: Lilly’s triple-G drug beats Ozempic in head-to-head study
stories.summary: Eli Lilly announced that its investigational drug retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic in a large diabetes study.

stories.title: ‘Ferritin face’: are social media claims about iron deficiency fact – or fiction?
stories.summary: Experts say symptoms such as dark circles under the eyes, grey skin, cracked lips and hair loss can be a warning sign – but there are other factors too TikTok is rife with influencers warning of “ferritin face”, a term they use to describe the pallor, dark circles, dry skin, and hair loss claimed…

stories.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
stories.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain.

stories.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
stories.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect.

stories.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging.

stories.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
stories.summary: The scientists involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.

stories.title: Give more people weight-loss jabs on the NHS, say MPs
stories.summary: Current plans for 6% of eligible patients to get Mounjaro by 2028 unambitious, say MPs.

stories.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
stories.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage.

stories.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates.

stories.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
stories.summary: Drugs will be tested simultaneously, which it's hoped will speed up the process of finding new treatments for this common type of dementia.

stories.title: Is it true that … you need to take 10,000 steps a day to be healthy?
stories.summary: The fitness benchmark has surprisingly unscientific origins – yet it does contain more than a kernel of truth The idea that we need to walk 10,000 steps a day originated not in medical research but in a 1960s marketing campaign for a pedometer, says Jack McNamara, senior lecturer in clinical…

stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
stories.summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet.

stories.title: Scientists find a youth protein that helps aging brain cells act young again
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a protein linked to youth helps protect the brain’s immune cells from age-related decline.

stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising two-way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, revealing how the brain carefully balances physical recovery with wakefulness.

stories.title: Decade-long gym steroids study shows just what happens to men's hearts
stories.summary: One of the first long-term studies that followed weight-training middle-aged men for nearly a decade has found that consistent use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) leads to the thickening of the heart’s left ventricular wall, which increasingly reduces the organ's ability to function.

stories.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
stories.summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days.

stories.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments
stories.summary: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process.

stories.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
stories.summary: A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood.
